source.title: Preliminary Results on Building Graphs from SAEs

record.file_problem: Some inline mathematical and numerical values are missing in the supplied text; the rest is readable.
record.tranche_reason: The post discusses feature splitting as motivation and says it may examine splitting and hierarchy in future work, but its reported results analyze conditional-dependence graphs rather than testing size-based SAE feature splitting.
record.gate_note: The reported outcomes concern graph stability, feature modules, and their relation to cosine similarity—not whether increasing dictionary size splits features or whether split features cover a parent's inputs. The graph findings are recorded as related results under fits_no_version.
record.test_reason: The post cites feature splitting and absorption as motivation and lists them as future work. Its results are conditional-dependence graphs over features of a single SAE (Gemma Scope layer 10, width 131k). There is no comparison across dictionary sizes, no parent-child firing analysis, no hierarchy test and no objective comparison, so no version is tested.
record.authors_conclusion: The record's paraphrase is accurate. The author presents this as a proof of concept: stable small modules look linguistically coherent and align only weakly with cosine similarity. The graph refines the activation-correlation structure; it is not a true precision graph or evidence of feature faithfulness.
record.recipe_differences: The post builds conditional-dependence graphs from SAE activations; it does not reproduce or test the original feature-splitting method.
record.method_sensitivity: The authors say the graph depends on correlation-based pre-screening and has hyperparameters that need more thorough sweeps or methodological changes. They use resampling of the same dataset, which they say does not establish feature faithfulness.

fits_no_version.finding: In Gemma2-27B layer 10 (Gemma Scope, width 131k), graph edge strength correlates only weakly with decoder cosine similarity, with high variance.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Conditional-dependence structure among SAE features is only weakly captured by decoder cosine similarity.

fits_no_version.finding: Resampling-stable graph edges form small standalone modules that look linguistically coherent. A set of tiny components consisted mostly of near-duplicate, high-cosine features.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Sparse conditional-dependence graphs over a single SAE's features reveal coherent modules and duplicated features.

record.problems: The authors describe the work as preliminary and note that it is not a true precision graph because SAE activations are not Gaussian. The method depends on correlation-based pre-screening and hyperparameters; only one null resampling per trial was used. Stability is measured by resampling the same dataset and does not establish feature faithfulness. The authors also say the 302-edge result at the stated FDR threshold is an extreme constraint. Some inline values are missing in the supplied text.
record.rows_left_out: The table of observed edges, expected null edges, and estimated FDR by repeat count is about graph-selection stability, not feature splitting or another version of the claim, so it was not included as a claim-relevant row.

untested.parts: All of it: no dictionary sizes compared.
All of it: a 27B model is used, but splitting itself is not measured.
All of it: hierarchy inference is listed as future work.
All of it: no absorption measurement.
All of it: no cross-size latent decomposition.
All of it: no objective comparison.

record.verdict_notes: The observation that tiny components are mostly duplicated, high-cosine features touches on feature redundancy. However, those features were filtered out and not quantified, and only one SAE size was studied, so it bears on no version.

versions.untested_parts: No comparison of SAE dictionary sizes or test of whether larger-dictionary features partition a smaller feature's inputs or lie near its direction.
Testing Gemma2:27b does not test whether splitting holds at scale or across SAE families.
The study identifies graph modules but does not test nested feature families or whether they mirror a representation hierarchy.
No parent-child firing comparison or test of changing SAE size or sparsity.
No comparison of larger- and smaller-SAE latents for decomposition or novelty.
No test attributing splitting to the SAE objective or comparing objectives such as Matryoshka SAEs.

rows.subject: gemma2:27b; Gemmascope, layer_10/width_131k
rows.operation_detail: Manually inspected connected components in a subset of stable graph edges.
rows.measure: Component structure and qualitative linguistic coherence
rows.value: The subset had one large connected component with 98 nodes, several smaller standalone components, and many tiny components. The smaller standalone components were described as linguistically coherent-looking; examples included possessive pronouns and context (9 nodes), “to be” and descriptive context (9 nodes), and negations with verb and article context (5 nodes).
rows.locator: Initial Results, Small components and Large component
rows.note: The study describes graph modules, not nested families produced by increasing SAE size. Some component-size values are missing from the supplied text.
rows.check: Correctly unlinked. It describes graph module structure within one SAE, not families arising from dictionary growth or a concept hierarchy. The record's component examples omit Component 4 (7 nodes) and Component 5 (5 nodes), which is minor.
